summary: 19-year-old student with 12 h of fever, headache, vomiting, neck stiffness, photophobia and a non-blanching purpuric rash; HR 128, BP 96/58.

inputs.hpi: University student living in halls. Twelve hours of fever, severe headache, vomiting and aching legs; now drowsy with a spreading rash on the legs that does not fade under a glass. Neck stiff, light hurts.

exam.general: Drowsy, cold hands and feet, capillary refill 4 s. Pulse 128/min, BP 96/58, RR 24, temperature 39.4°C, SpO2 96%.
exam.neuro: GCS 13, neck stiffness, Kernig sign positive, no focal deficit.
exam.skin: Non-blanching petechial and purpuric rash on both legs and trunk.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Meningococcal meningitis with septicaemia (suspected)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected meningococcal disease (non-blanching rash, meningism, shock): IV ceftriaxone now, blood cultures, do not delay for LP.

mustInclude.note: Graded as management because the web sepsis prompt adds blood cultures as a plan line; the seeded investigation lists come from unrelated PANE protocols.

guideline.name: NICE NG240 — Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Suspected bacterial meningitis or meningococcal disease: IV ceftriaxone without delay (do not delay for lumbar puncture or imaging); blood cultures; dexamethasone for suspected bacterial meningitis; senior/critical care review; public health notification
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG240. London: NICE; 2024.

guideline.name: NICE NG51 — Suspected sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management
guideline.section: High-risk criteria (new confusion, SBP ≤90, HR >130, RR ≥25, lactate); blood cultures and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour for high risk; IV fluid bolus; lactate; senior review; source control
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management. NICE guideline NG51 (updated 2024). London: NICE.

rationale: NICE NG240: IV ceftriaxone immediately without waiting for LP/imaging, blood cultures, dexamethasone, public health notification.
